This solution would comply with the GDScript standards. Users would not think of it as out of place or as non-intuitive, since the proposal would follow the same syntax as if-statements and function definitions.

This solution only renders the already complicated task of writing multi-threaded applications clearer for all users, it is needed, and is not a simple syntax preference.

This solution fits GDScript's philosophy of being a python-like language that doesn't get in the way of the developers and let them focus on making games, unlike the method that's currently implemented.

Perhaps a GDScript macro addon could solve this issue, but such addons I've found only _generated_ proper GDScript code, similar to YASnippet. It did not fundamentally change how GDScript is written, unlike C or Lisp macros.

Also, mutexes are almost mandatory and certainly plentiful when writing multi-threaded applications, it is one of the first things that is taught in the [official Godot Docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/threads/using_multiple_threads.html#mutexes).
